module.title: Explaining Reasons & Consequences: 'Because' & 'So'
module.objective: Connect clauses to explain reasons and consequences in daily conversation using conjunctions 'because' and 'so'.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Reasons and Results at the Park
subModules.grammarFocus: Using because for reasons and so for results
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Everyday problems, feelings, travel, and weather

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will read a short story about two friends at the park. You will find reasons with because and results with so. These words help you understand why things happen and what happens next.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use because to give a reason: result + because + reason. Use so to show a result: reason + so + result.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words for transport, weather, feelings, plans, and everyday problems.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: First, skim the text to find the main idea. Then, scan for because and so to connect each reason and result.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short passage about friends and plans.
Identify key details about time, weather, travel, and feelings.
Recognize because for reasons and so for results in a reading text.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your bus is late. What can you say?
options: I may be late because the bus is late.
I may be late so the bus is late.
I may be late because so the bus is late.
contextWarmup.explanation: The bus is late is the reason. Use because to explain why you may be late.

rules: Use because to introduce the reason: I am tired because I ran.
Use so to introduce the result: I ran, so I am tired.
Do not use because and so together in the same sentence.

commonTrap.explanation: A common mistake is using because and so together. Choose one connector and put the reason and result in the correct order.
commonTrap.wrong: I was late, so because I missed the bus.
commonTrap.correct: I was late because I missed the bus. / I missed the bus, so I was late.

content.contractionsTitle: Natural Spoken Contractions: Reasons and Results
content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how subjects and verbs smoothly merge in natural spoken English:

contractions.subject: I
contractions.exampleFull: I am late because the bus is slow.
contractions.exampleContracted: I'm late because the bus is slow.

contractions.subject: He
contractions.exampleFull: He is tired, so he sits down.
contractions.exampleContracted: He's tired, so he sits down.

contractions.subject: They
contractions.exampleFull: They are happy because the weather is sunny.
contractions.exampleContracted: They're happy because the weather is sunny.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Structure with Because and So
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble and swap sentence blocks to explore affirmative, negative, and question patterns:
complements: late because the bus is slow
happy because my friend is here

items.collocation: There is heavy traffic this morning.
The bus is late because of traffic.
I wait for the bus every day.
She sends her friend a message.
We arrive at the park at ten.

What is the reason for your message?
Missing the bus is the result of oversleeping.

sections.title: Reading Passage: A Morning at the Park

content.context: Mia and Leo want to meet at the park, but Mia has a problem on the way.
content.text: On Saturday, Mia plans to meet her friend Leo at the park. She leaves home at ten o’clock, but the bus is late because there is heavy traffic. Mia waits for twenty minutes, so she sends Leo a message. “I’m sorry. I may be late because the bus is not here.” Leo reads the message and buys two sandwiches. The weather is sunny, so he sits under a tree near the park gate. At last, Mia arrives at eleven. She is tired because she runs from the bus stop. Leo gives her a sandwich, so she feels better. They do not play football because Mia is exhausted. Instead, they walk slowly and talk about their week. Mia is happy because Leo understands. They enjoy the morning, so they plan another park day next Saturday.

highlights.note: Because introduces the reason for the late bus.

highlights.text: so she sends Leo a message
highlights.note: So introduces the result of waiting for the bus.
Heavy traffic means there are many cars on the road.

gistQuestion.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Mia and Leo meet at the park after Mia has travel problems.
Mia and Leo play football for many hours.
Leo misses the bus on his way to the park.
gistQuestion.explanation: The passage is about Mia's late bus, her meeting with Leo, and their quiet time at the park.

detailQuestions.explanation: The text says that the bus is late because there is heavy traffic.

detailQuestions.prompt: What does Mia do after she waits for twenty minutes?
detailQuestions.explanation: Mia waits for twenty minutes, so she sends Leo a message.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why do Mia and Leo not play football?
detailQuestions.explanation: They do not play football because Mia is exhausted.

questions.question: What time does Mia arrive at the park?
questions.explanation: The passage says, “At last, Mia arrives at eleven.”

questions.question: Why does Leo sit under a tree?
questions.explanation: The weather is sunny, so Leo sits under a tree near the park gate.

questions.question: What does Leo give Mia?
questions.explanation: Leo buys two sandwiches and gives Mia one sandwich when she arrives.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly shows a reason from the passage?
options: Mia is tired because she runs from the bus stop.
Mia is tired so she runs from the bus stop.
Mia is tired because so she runs from the bus stop.
questions.explanation: Mia runs from the bus stop first, and this is the reason she is tired. Use because to introduce the reason.

questions.question: What do Mia and Leo plan at the end of the passage?
options: A bus trip to another town.
questions.explanation: They enjoy the morning, so they plan another park day next Saturday.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Weekend Plans and Weather

content.summary: In this listening mission, you will hear Emma and Tom talk about a changed weekend plan. Listen for because to hear a reason. Listen for so to hear a result or consequence. The reason often comes after because, and the result often comes after so.
learningObjectives: Identify reasons in a short conversation by listening for because.
Identify results and consequences in a short conversation by listening for so.
Understand simple weekend plans, weather, and time information in spoken English.

keyPhrases.note: Use because to give the reason for an action or situation.

keyPhrases.phrase: It was raining, so we cancelled the picnic.
keyPhrases.note: Use so to introduce the result of a situation.

keyPhrases.phrase: I am free on Saturday because I finished my homework.
keyPhrases.meaning: Saya bebas pada hari Sabtu karena saya sudah menyelesaikan pekerjaan rumah saya.
keyPhrases.note: The second part explains why the speaker is free.

keyPhrases.phrase: The weather forecast is good, so we can go hiking.
keyPhrases.meaning: Prakiraan cuacanya bagus, jadi kami bisa pergi mendaki.
keyPhrases.note: The first part gives the cause, and the part after so gives the result.

keyPhrases.phrase: Let's meet at 8 AM because we need to start early.
keyPhrases.meaning: Mari bertemu pukul 8 pagi karena kita harus mulai lebih awal.
keyPhrases.note: Use because to explain why you suggest a time.

connectedSpeech.note: The final sound in because links smoothly to I. Listen for because-I as one connected sound group.
In natural speech, can is often weak and sounds like /kən/.
Was is often reduced to /wəz/ in normal conversation.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: A New Weekend Plan

content.context: Emma and Tom talk about their weekend plans. Their plans changed because of bad weather, but they make a new plan for next Saturday.
content.audioPrompt: Listen carefully to the following dialogue between Emma and Tom. Listen for the reasons after because and the results after so.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Hi Tom! Why didn't you come to the park yesterday?
lines.translation: Hai Tom! Mengapa kamu tidak datang ke taman kemarin?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I didn't come because the weather was terrible. It was raining all day!
lines.translation: Aku tidak datang karena cuacanya sangat buruk. Hujan sepanjang hari!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Yes, I know. It was raining, so we cancelled the picnic too.
lines.translation: Ya, aku tahu. Hujan, jadi kami juga membatalkan piknik.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's a shame! Why don't we plan something for next weekend?
lines.translation: Sayang sekali! Bagaimana kalau kita merencanakan sesuatu untuk akhir pekan depan?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Good idea! I'm free on Saturday because I finished all my homework.
lines.translation: Ide bagus! Aku bebas pada hari Sabtu karena aku sudah menyelesaikan semua pekerjaan rumahku.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Perfect! The weather forecast is good, so we can go hiking.
lines.translation: Sempurna! Prakiraan cuacanya bagus, jadi kita bisa pergi mendaki.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: I love hiking! I'm excited because I haven't been hiking for months.
lines.translation: Aku suka mendaki! Aku senang karena sudah berbulan-bulan aku tidak mendaki.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Me too! Let's meet at 8 AM because we need to start early.
lines.translation: Aku juga! Mari bertemu pukul 8 pagi karena kita harus mulai lebih awal.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Give Reasons and Results

content.summary: Use because to give a reason. Use so to show a result. Both words join two complete clauses. A complete clause has a subject and a verb.

blueprintItems.title: Write the Result First with Because
blueprintItems.example: I am tired because I worked late.

blueprintItems.title: Write the Reason First with So
blueprintItems.example: I worked late, so I am tired.

blueprintItems.title: Check Both Clauses
blueprintItems.example: She is happy because she has a new bike.

blueprintItems.title: Answer Why Questions
blueprintItems.example: Why are you late? Because the bus is slow.

mechanicsRules.rule: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i stay home because it is raining.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I stay home because it is raining.
mechanicsRules.why: The first word in a sentence needs a capital letter. The word I is always a capital letter.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a comma before so when it joins two complete clauses.
mechanicsRules.badExample: It is raining so I stay home.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: It is raining, so I stay home.
mechanicsRules.why: The comma helps the reader see the reason first and the result after so.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not usually use a comma before because.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I stay home, because it is raining.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I stay home because it is raining.
mechanicsRules.why: Because connects the result to its reason without a comma in a simple sentence.

mechanicsRules.rule: Finish a complete sentence with a full stop.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She is happy because she has a new bike
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She is happy because she has a new bike.
mechanicsRules.why: A full stop shows that the sentence is complete.

sampleSentences.en: I wear a coat because it is cold.
sampleSentences.id: English meaning: I wear a coat for a cold day.

sampleSentences.en: It is cold, so I wear a coat.
sampleSentences.id: English meaning: The cold weather causes me to wear a coat.

sampleSentences.en: She is smiling because she likes the gift.
sampleSentences.id: English meaning: She likes the gift, and this makes her smile.

sampleSentences.en: The shop is closed, so we go home.
sampleSentences.id: English meaning: The closed shop causes us to go home.

mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use capital I and add a full stop at the end.

mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: She is sad because her cat is sick.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Do not use a comma before because in this simple sentence.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: My Reason
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write two sentences about your day. Use because in one sentence. Give a result and a reason.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I am happy because my friend is here. I drink water because I am thirsty.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: What Happens Next?
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write two sentences with so. Write the reason first, then write the result. Use a comma before so.
guidedLabChallenges.example: It is raining, so I take an umbrella. I have homework, so I stay at home.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write one complete sentence about why you are happy, tired, hungry, or sad. Use because.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write one complete sentence. Use because correctly. Include a subject and a verb on both sides of because. Use a capital letter and a full stop.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I am happy because I have a new book.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write one complete sentence about rain, cold weather, or being late. Use so.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write one complete sentence. Put the reason before so and the result after so. Use a comma before so, a capital letter, and a full stop.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: It is raining, so I take an umbrella.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write two connected sentences about your day. Use because in one sentence and so in the other sentence.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write at least two complete sentences. Use because for a reason and so for a result. Check capitals, the comma before so, and full stops.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I am tired because I studied last night. I have a test today, so I study again.

content.summary: Use because to give a reason and so to give a result. Speak in short, clear sentences. Pause a little before because or so to make your meaning easy to understand.
content.audioGuidance: Say because as /bɪˈkɔːz/ with stress on the second part: be-CAUSE. In a sentence, because and so are usually not very strong. Put more voice stress on important words, such as tired, late, alarm, and rest. Use a falling voice at the end of a complete answer.

pillars.name: Clear Reasons
pillars.target: Use because to answer why questions
pillars.explanation: Say the result first, then add because and the reason. Example: I am tired because I stayed up late.

pillars.name: Clear Results
pillars.target: Use so to show a consequence
pillars.explanation: Say the cause first, then add so and the result. Example: I overslept, so I missed breakfast.

pillars.name: Voice Stress
pillars.target: Stress key words in your message
pillars.explanation: Make important words stronger and clearer. In I am tired because I stayed up late, stress tired and late.

pillars.name: Natural Intonation
pillars.explanation: Use rising intonation for a yes-no question, such as Did you eat breakfast? Use falling intonation for an answer, such as No, I did not.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: As a noun, REcord means saved information. As a verb, re-CORD means to save sound or video. The stressed syllable changes.
As a noun, PREsent is a gift. As a verb, pre-SENT means to show or give something. The stressed syllable changes.

drills.targetText: I am tired because I stayed up late.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ əm ˈtaɪərd bɪˈkɔːz aɪ steɪd ʌp leɪt/
drills.focus: Stress the important words tired, because, and late.
drills.hint: Say because in three parts: be-CAUSE. Make CAUSE stronger.

drills.targetText: I overslept, so I missed breakfast.
drills.focus: Pause briefly before so and stress missed breakfast.
drills.hint: Keep so short and connect it smoothly to the next words.

drills.targetText: My alarm did not go off, so I was late.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ əˈlɑːrm dɪd nɒt ɡoʊ ɔːf soʊ aɪ wəz leɪt/
drills.focus: Use clear final sounds in alarm, off, and late.
drills.hint: Make your voice fall at the end of the sentence.

drills.targetText: I am going home early because I need to rest.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ əm ˈɡoʊɪŋ hoʊm ˈɜːrli bɪˈkɔːz aɪ niːd tə rɛst/
drills.focus: Stress home early, because, and rest.
drills.hint: Do not rush. Take a small pause before because.

roleplay.context: You are talking with Mr. Khoirul about yesterday, this morning, and your plans after class. Explain reasons with because and results with so.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Good morning! You look tired today. Why are you tired?
turns.translation: Selamat pagi! Kamu terlihat lelah hari ini. Mengapa kamu lelah?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Khoirul! I am tired because I stayed up late studying last night.
turns.translation: Selamat pagi, Pak Khoirul! Saya lelah karena saya begadang belajar tadi malam.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: I see. What happened this morning? Did you have breakfast?
turns.translation: Saya mengerti. Apa yang terjadi pagi ini? Apakah kamu sarapan?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I overslept this morning, so I did not have time for breakfast.
turns.translation: Saya kesiangan pagi ini, jadi saya tidak punya waktu untuk sarapan.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Oh no! That is not good. Why did you oversleep?
turns.translation: Oh tidak! Itu tidak baik. Mengapa kamu kesiangan?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I overslept because my alarm did not go off. I forgot to set it.
turns.translation: Saya kesiangan karena alarm saya tidak berbunyi. Saya lupa memasangnya.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That happens sometimes. What are your plans after class today?
turns.translation: Itu kadang-kadang terjadi. Apa rencanamu setelah kelas hari ini?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I am going home early because I need to rest. I am really exhausted.
turns.translation: Saya akan pulang lebih awal karena saya perlu beristirahat. Saya sangat lelah.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Talk about a time when you were tired. Speak for 20 to 30 seconds. Use because and so.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please tell me why you were tired and what happened because of it.
storyPoints: Explain why you were tired with because.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I was tired because I stayed up late, so I went to bed early.

practicumQuestions.hint: Speak slowly and stress the reason and the result.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task checks if you can connect a reason and a consequence in a short personal story.

practicumQuestions.hint: Pause a little before because and so.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task checks if you can explain a simple sequence of cause and result.

practicumQuestions.explanation: Use because to give a direct reason after a why question.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Reply to Mr. Khoirul. Tell him why you are going home early.

practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ əm ˈɡoʊɪŋ hoʊm ˈɜːrli bɪˈkɔːz aɪ niːd tə rɛst/
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task checks if you can explain your plan with a clear reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Reply to your friend. Explain your new plan because of the rain.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: It is raining now. What will you do?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You want to go to the park, but it is raining. Your friend asks about your plan.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are talking to a friend. Say that you will stay home and explain why.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: It is raining, so I will stay home.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈreɪnɪŋ soʊ aɪ wɪl steɪ hoʊm/
practicumQuestions.hint: Keep so short and say stay home clearly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This task checks if you can use so to explain a change of plan.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the sentence. Use the word exhausted for very tired.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Complete and say: I am going home early because I am ____.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I am going home early because I am exhausted.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ əm ˈɡoʊɪŋ hoʊm ˈɜːrli bɪˈkɔːz aɪ əm ɪɡˈzɔːstɪd/
practicumQuestions.hint: Say exhausted in three parts: ex-HAUS-ted.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Exhausted means very tired. It is useful when you explain why you need to rest.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the sentence with because. Put the reason after because.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Join these ideas: I was late. I missed the bus.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I was late because I missed the bus.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wəz leɪt bɪˈkɔːz aɪ mɪst ðə bʌs/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use because before the reason, not before the result.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Because connects an action or situation with its reason.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say both words clearly. Notice that the stressed syllable changes.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I have a REcord, and I reCORD my voice.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˈrɛkərd ænd aɪ rɪˈkɔːrd maɪ vɔɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the noun, stress RE. For the verb, stress CORD.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Some English words change stress when they change from a noun to a verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ask the question with rising intonation. Then say the answer with falling intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say: Did you eat breakfast? No, I did not, because I overslept.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Did you eat breakfast? No, I did not, because I overslept.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /dɪd juː iːt ˈbrɛkfəst | noʊ aɪ dɪd nɒt bɪˈkɔːz aɪ ˌoʊvərˈslɛpt/
practicumQuestions.hint: Let your voice rise at breakfast in the question and fall at overslept in the answer.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Yes-no questions usually have rising intonation. Complete statements usually have falling intonation.
